evaluation.overall_comment: The Korean translation captures the overall tone of a spoken dialogue and renders most technical terms correctly, but it suffers from serious structural and linguistic problems. Large portions of the original script (the discussion on Heisenberg’s principle, diffraction, Abbe limit, NSOM, and the concluding philosophical question) are missing or severely truncated, breaking line‑to‑line correspondence and causing loss of propositional content. Several lines end abruptly, leaving sentences incomplete. Moreover, the text contains stray Chinese characters (e.g., “确立”) and an Arabic fragment (“گوید”), which violate the target‑language requirement and script consistency. While speaker labels are present and consistent, the mismatched attribution and missing sections mean the translation cannot be used as a faithful rendition of the original. A revised version should keep every line in order, complete all sentences, eliminate foreign‐language intrusions, and ensure that no content is omitted.
